drhp.business: Sinclairs Hotels Limited owns and operates hotels and resorts in India, serving domestic leisure travellers, destination weddings, conferences and corporate/MICE guests. The Company describes itself as a trusted and home-grown hospitality brand known for quality service, strong food offerings, hygienic operations and transparent business practices. As on March 31, 2026 it had a presence across ten destinations within the country and was in the process of further expansion, including through properties taken on lease.

risks.note: The hospitality business is exposed to macroeconomic fluctuations, inflationary pressures and changes in discretionary consumer spending; any slowdown in economic growth could affect demand across leisure and business segments.
Adverse weather conditions at key tourist destinations can impact seasonality and occupancy levels — structurally relevant given the Company's leisure-destination footprint.
risks.risk: Weather and seasonality at key tourist destinations

risks.note: Rising costs relating to power, fuel, food inputs and employee expenses may impact operating margins.
High taxation levels and denial of input GST in hotel's room revenues pose a structural drag on hotel economics that the Company cannot control.
risks.risk: Tax structure — high taxation and denial of input GST on room revenues

risks.note: Regulatory changes and competitive intensity in certain markets are flagged as challenges to the business.
Geo-political developments or any disruption in travel sentiment could affect demand across leisure and business segments.
risks.risk: Geo-political developments and disruption in travel sentiment

risks.note: The Directors' Report states that the policy on risk management is not applicable to the Company; mitigation relies on a proactive management approach — dynamic pricing, cost controls, manpower deployment, multi-skilling and monitoring of operating metrics — rather than a formal framework.
risks.risk: No formal risk management policy at company level

sk.overview: The overnight ocean and coastal cruise industry in India is a nascent, high-growth segment of cruise tourism. Per the issuer-commissioned CRISIL Report (May 2026), the domestic market was valued at approximately Rs 8,301 million in Fiscal 2025 (up from Rs 5,764 million in Fiscal 2020, ~8% CAGR) but is estimated to have declined ~12% to Rs 7,325 million in Fiscal 2026 amid macro/fuel/geopolitical headwinds, before a projected sharp expansion.
